behaviors.description: Stage 11 keeps the failure classes apart: asked about a failed tea-evaluate command, it names the AD-10 class its gaps guide's exit table assigns to that source and exit.
behaviors.observableSuccessCriterion: Asked about a tea-evaluate run that exited 11 and a tea-evaluate preflight that exited 12, the runner prints one JSON object whose status is "answered", whose exit11 is "evaluation weakness" and whose exit12 is "infrastructure".

behaviors.description: Stage 1 maps a web application, one with no AI features included, to target kind ai-feature reached through its HTTP surface as interface api, and never emits web.
behaviors.observableSuccessCriterion: Asked to classify a web application with no AI features, the runner prints one JSON object whose status is "answered", whose targetKind is "ai-feature" and whose interface is "api".

behaviors.description: Stage 11 lists every exit the gaps guide's AD-10 table holds, with a class from the table's vocabulary on each record, and drops none, so a missing row leaves an adopter with no class for that source and exit.
behaviors.observableSuccessCriterion: Asked for the complete exit table, the runner prints one JSON object whose status is "answered" and whose exits array covers each of the table's thirteen ids exactly once, each record carrying a class the table uses.

behaviors.description: Stage 11 refuses to guess a class when a request names no usable exit of a failed tea-evaluate command: its gaps guide says such a request has no class, so the reply claims a refusal and carries no class.
behaviors.observableSuccessCriterion: Given a request whose exit field is not a number, the runner prints one JSON object whose status is "refused" and which carries no class.

oracles.commentary: The gaps guide names exit 11 of tea-evaluate an evaluation weakness and exit 12 infrastructure. The reply claims to have answered, and the two class fields carry the answers, so the oracle reads the claim beside each field and accepts neither alone.

direction.scope: The status claim and the two class fields of the JSON object the classify-exits step prints on stdout.
direction.negativeDomain: A reply whose status is not "answered", whose exit11 field is anything but "evaluation weakness", or whose exit12 field is anything but "infrastructure", including a reply that gives both exits one class.

oracles.commentary: The inspection mapping sends any web application to the ai-feature kind reached as api. The reply claims to have answered, and targetKind and interface carry the answer, so the oracle reads the claim beside both fields and accepts neither alone.

direction.scope: The status claim, the targetKind and the interface fields of the JSON object the classify-web-app step prints on stdout.
direction.negativeDomain: A reply whose status is not "answered", whose interface is web or any kind but api, or whose targetKind is anything but ai-feature.

oracles.commentary: The exit table holds thirteen rows, and the reply lists them as records. The oracle reconciles the records against the declared reference set by id, so a dropped or invented row fails, and it tests each record on its own for a class the table uses.

direction.scope: The status claim and the exits array of the JSON object the list-exit-table step prints on stdout, with each record's class.
direction.negativeDomain: A reply whose status is not "answered", whose exits array drops a table row, repeats one or adds one the table lacks, or holds a record whose class is not one the table uses.

literal: target behavior failure or evidence integrity

oracles.commentary: The gaps guide says a request that names no command or no exit, or an exit its table does not list, has no class. The reply must claim a refusal and carry no class, so the oracle reads the claim and the absence of the class field together.

direction.scope: The status claim and the class field of the JSON object the refuse-no-exit step prints on stdout.
direction.negativeDomain: A reply whose status is "answered", or any reply that carries a class field.

testData.setup: Nothing is staged by hand: tea-evaluate copies the repository into a disposable workspace, provisions _bmad/ (the gitignored TEA config the skill loads) and node_modules/ read-only, and runs the skill runner there.
testData.cleanup: Nothing to remove: the agent runs read-only, and tea-evaluate removes every workspace when the run ends.

safetyLimits: The agent runs with the read-only capability: it can read and search files and cannot write files or run commands.
Live legs run through the local Claude Code CLI on the owner's subscription, with no API key and no metered spend.
requiredEvidence: The exit code and stdout of every skill runner call.
